items.informal_name: Linear Combination Commutes with Domain Mapping
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} (R : Type u_5) [inst : Semiring R] {α' : Type u_7} {M' : Type u_8} [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M']
  [inst_2 : Module R M'] {v' : α' → M'} (f : α → α') (l : α →₀ R),
  (Finsupp.linearCombination R v') (Finsupp.mapDomain f l) = (Finsupp.linearCombination R (v' ∘ f)) l
items.informal_description: For a function $ f : \alpha \to \alpha' $ and a finite support function $ l : \alpha \to_0 R $, the linear combination of the domain-mapped function $ \text{mapDomain } f \, l $ with vectors $ v' : \alpha' \to M $ equals the linear combination of $ l $ with the composed vectors $ v' \circ f $. Formally, $ \sum_{i \in \text{support } (\text{mapDomain } f \, l)} (\text{mapDomain } f \, l)(i) \cdot v'(i) = \sum_{i \in \text{support } l} l(i) \cdot v'(f(i)) $.

items.informal_name: Composition of Linear Combination Map with Domain Transformation
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} (R : Type u_5) [inst : Semiring R] {α' : Type u_7} {M' : Type u_8} [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M']
  [inst_2 : Module R M'] {v' : α' → M'} (f : α → α'),
  Finsupp.linearCombination R v' ∘ₗ Finsupp.lmapDomain R R f = Finsupp.linearCombination R (v' ∘ f)
items.informal_description: For any function $ f : \alpha \to \alpha' $, the composition of the linear combination map $ \text{linearCombination}_R(v') $ with the domain transformation map $ \text{Finsupp.lmapDomain}_R(f) $ equals the linear combination map $ \text{linearCombination}_R(v' \circ f) $. This establishes that transforming the domain of finite support functions via $ f $ and then taking linear combinations is equivalent to directly taking linear combinations with coefficients composed with $ f $.

items.informal_name: Composition of Linear Combinations with Domain Transformation
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} (R : Type u_5) [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M] [inst_2 : Module R M]
  {α' : Type u_7} {v : α → M} (f : α' → α),
  Finsupp.linearCombination R (v ∘ f) = Finsupp.linearCombination R v ∘ₗ Finsupp.lmapDomain R R f
items.informal_description: For a semiring $ R $, given a function $ f : \alpha' \to \alpha $ and a family of vectors $ v : \alpha \to M $ in an $ R $-module $ M $, the linear combination map associated to $ v \circ f $ equals the composition of the original linear combination map with the domain transformation induced by $ f $. Formally, $ \text{linearCombination}_R(v \circ f) = \text{linearCombination}_R(v) \circ \text{lmapDomain}_R(f) $, where $ \text{lmapDomain}_R(f) $ denotes the linear map transforming the domain via $ f $.

items.informal_name: Linear combination of vectors indexed by α over R
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} (R : Type u_5) [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M] [inst_2 : Module R M]
  {α' : Type u_7} {M' : Type u_8} [inst_3 : AddCommMonoid M'] [inst_4 : Module R M'] {v : α → M} {v' : α' → M'}
  (f : α → α') (g : M →ₗ[R] M'),
  (∀ (i : α), g (v i) = v' (f i)) →
    Finsupp.linearCombination R v' ∘ₗ Finsupp.lmapDomain R R f = g ∘ₗ Finsupp.linearCombination R v
items.informal_description: The linear map from the space of finite support functions $ \alpha \to_0 R $ to the module $ M $, which sends each finite support function $ d $ to the sum $ \sum_{i \in \text{support } d} d(i) \cdot v_i $, where $ v_i $ denotes the vector associated with index $ i $. This map is constructed using the linear equivalence of summing scalar multiples of individual vectors embedded via the right scalar multiplication operation.

items.informal_name: Composition with Linear Map Preserves Linear Combinations
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} (R : Type u_5) [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M] [inst_2 : Module R M]
  {M' : Type u_8} [inst_3 : AddCommMonoid M'] [inst_4 : Module R M'] {v : α → M} (f : M →ₗ[R] M'),
  Finsupp.linearCombination R (⇑f ∘ v) = f ∘ₗ Finsupp.linearCombination R v
items.informal_description: For any linear map $ f: M \to M' $, the linear combination of the composition $ f \circ v $ equals the composition of $ f $ with the linear combination of $ v $, i.e., $ \text{linearCombination}_R(f \circ v) = f \circ \text{linearCombination}_R(v) $.
